findings.reason: The protected source is a clear iterative topological solution: it computes outgoing edges to larger neighbors, queues local maxima, and peels reverse-DAG layers without recursion. Coordinate and graph-state names are genuine concepts, control flow is direct, and no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 329 and its Python longestIncreasingPath surface. The Reference preserves four-direction adjacency, strict increase, forbidden diagonals and wraparound, all three source examples, both source diagrams, and all four constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064398695. Its Solution.longestIncreasingPath body structurally aligns with the protected app-local solve body: dimensions, outdegree construction, maximum queue, reverse-edge decrements, and layer count are identical apart from the class wrapper and legacy List annotation.

The legal 32, 64, and 128-cell increasing-row tiers span 4x and make all starting cells share suffix paths. The current source passes all nine executions at +0.01 relative growth and 1.00x; correct uncached DFS passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +1.01 and 7.90x.
The Approach exactly proves that strict increases form a DAG, derives reverse topological peeling from local maxima, relates each layer to continuation length, and gives O(mn) time and O(mn) space.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including all three source examples and explanation status, all four constraints, movement restrictions, and independently rendered diagrams corresponding to both source visuals.
